rationale: Cortex is the bulk of the adrenal gland, so little dilution expected.
Breast tissue is largely adipose and stroma; luminal epithelium is a small fraction.
Cholangiocytes line bile ducts inside liver but are a small percentage of liver cells. Strong dilution expected.
Transverse colon is mucosa-bearing (D40); epithelium is well represented.
Stratified squamous mucosa, matched to oesophageal mucosa as in the Step 4 map.
Proximal tubule dominates renal cortex.
Same lineage and tissue as clear cell.
Hepatocytes are the bulk of liver; minimal dilution expected.
AT2 cells are a minority of lung tissue by cell count.
Airway basal cells are a small fraction of whole lung.
Pancreas is overwhelmingly acinar; ductal cells are a few percent. Strong dilution expected.
Chromaffin cells sit in the medulla, a minority of the adrenal gland. Strong dilution expected.
Glandular epithelium is well represented in prostate tissue.
Same lineage as colon; transverse colon used for the mucosal layer (D40).
Melanocytes are a small fraction of skin, which is mostly keratinocytes.
Gastric mucosa is well represented in the GTEx stomach sample.
Germ cells at various stages dominate adult testis.
Follicular cells are the bulk of thyroid.
GTEx uterus is whole myometrium-dominated wall; endometrium is a minority. Dilution expected.
Uveal melanocytes have no GTEx tissue; cutaneous melanocytes in skin are the closest available lineage match, as in the Step 4 map.
LGG spans astrocytoma and oligodendroglioma; a single origin would be a forced choice.
Squamous and adenocarcinoma are both common. GTEx cervix has 4-6 samples, so oesophageal mucosa stands in as stratified squamous epithelium, as in D40.
TCGA ESCA pools squamous carcinoma and Barrett-associated adenocarcinoma, which have different origins.
The cell of origin is actively contested between astrocyte, oligodendrocyte precursor and neural stem cell.
TCGA SARC pools leiomyosarcoma, liposarcoma, UPS and others with different origins. No single lineage applies.
Biphasic by definition, with both epithelial and mesenchymal components.

DLBCL arises in lymph node, which GTEx does not sample. Spleen was considered and rejected: it is a lymphoid organ but not the tissue this tumour comes from, so a shift measured against it would not mean what the column says it means.
Origin in the distal nephron is accepted, but collecting ducts are largely medullary and GTEx samples cortex only.
Mesothelium is a single cell layer on serosal surfaces. No GTEx tissue represents it; visceral adipose contains some but is not mesothelium.
Current consensus places the origin in fallopian tube epithelium. GTEx Fallopian Tube has 5 samples, below the 10-sample floor (D37).
